title: How Discord Stores Trillions of Messages Without Slowing Down — Engineering Cheat Sheet
subtitle: Scaling extreme message volume using Cassandra, sharding, and optimized data modeling.
summary: Discord migrated from MongoDB to Apache Cassandra to handle massive write throughput and ensure linear scalability. This architectural shift leverages intelligent row-key design and physical data partitioning to maintain low latency across trillions of records.

key_concepts.name: Cassandra Partitioning
key_concepts.detail: Data is sharded by channel_id, grouping related messages together on the same physical nodes to ensure sequential disk reads and efficient query performance at petabyte scale.

key_concepts.name: Time-Bucket Partitioning
key_concepts.detail: Each partition contains messages within a specific time range to prevent partition hotspots and manage heap memory overhead, enabling fast lookups even as message history grows indefinitely.

key_concepts.name: Write Path Optimization
key_concepts.detail: Discord leverages Cassandra's LSM-tree architecture, which converts random writes into sequential disk I/O via Memtables and SSTables, bypassing the heavy locking overhead common in traditional B-Tree databases.

code_cheatsheet.explanation: Runs post-compaction cleanup to remove keys no longer belonging to the node after a cluster topology change.
Composite key construction pattern to distribute data evenly across the cluster while ensuring range-based queries remain performant.

best_practices: Avoid wide partitions; keep bucket sizes limited to prevent JVM garbage collection pauses.
Prioritize sequential I/O patterns by aligning data models with query access paths.
Implement robust observability to track compaction stress and SSTable read latency.
Choose eventually consistent reads only when necessary to favor high availability and write throughput.

interview_qa.question: Why did Discord switch from MongoDB to Cassandra for message storage?
interview_qa.answer: MongoDB's write throughput hit a ceiling due to index size and replication lag, while Cassandra's LSM-tree storage engine supports high-concurrency writes and linear horizontal scaling. Cassandra avoids the lock contention found in traditional databases, allowing Discord to maintain performance as data cardinality explodes.
